rfi.title: France's Sophie Adenot returns to the void for second spacewalk in a week
rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot on Tuesday stepped outside the International Space Station (ISS) for the second time, a week after she became the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Adenot and US astronaut Anil Menon are due to finish replacing a faulty antenna on the ISS after running out of time during their first spacewalk on 18 August.

rfi.title: Looking up: French radio enthusiast captures ISS signals from his garage
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the second episode of a five-part series, RFI hears from Vincent Plousey, a radio ham from Tavaux in eastern France whose hobby is picking up signals from the ISS using homemade antennas built in his garage.

rfi.title: Survivors of Guinea's deadly landfill collapse say authorities ignored warnings
rfi.description: Two days after a deadly landfill collapse in Guinea, rescuers are using giant excavators to search for victims. Anger is rising among residents, who say they had warned authorities that the rubbish dump was precarious.

rfi.title: US and Denmark push for nationwide expansion of UN arms embargo in Sudan
rfi.description: The United States on Monday urged the United Nations Security Council to expand an arms embargo on the Sudanese region of Darfur to cover all of Sudan, saying the nation's brutal conflict risks regional expansion. The suggestion was supported by Denmark, which holds the Council's rotating presidency.

rfi.title: At least 40 killed as gangs attack displaced people near Haiti capital
rfi.description: At least 40 people have been killed, some execution-style, after gangs attacked displaced people sheltering in a church near Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince at the weekend, local authorities said.

rfi.title: French village reels from tornado that damaged hundreds of homes
rfi.description: Hundreds of damaged homes, widespread power cuts and blocked roads confronted residents of southwestern France on Tuesday after a tornado tore through the village of Pomas, injuring 39 people, two of them critically.

rfi.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
rfi.description: Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry.

rfi.title: Ukraine's allies pledge to continue support with focus on air defence
rfi.description: Ukraine's allies on Monday pledged to keep up their support in the war against Russia, with a renewed focus on air defence investment to counter a shortage of US Patriot interceptors.

rfi.title: Saudi Arabia to invest €6bn in building theme parks near Paris
rfi.description: France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed a memo of understanding for a €6 billion Saudi investment to create three theme parks near Paris, the office of the French president said.

rfi.title: Mediterranean migrant rescue ships threatened by Libyan groups, warns NGO
rfi.description: A leading group monitoring and providing aid to migrants crossing the Mediterranean have warned that its rescue ships have been facing increasing threats and harassment from Libyan groups.

rfi.title: Malian PM's visit to Algeria underlines need for mutual security goals
rfi.description: The acting head of the Malian government, General Abdoulaye Maiga has begun a two-day visit to Algeria. It comes amid a thaw after months of tension. RFI spoke to Bakary Sambe, the Director of the Timbuktu Institute about the security situation and what the countries hope to gain from the meeting.

rfi.title: Six million Somalis face acute hunger as drought and conflict worsen
rfi.description: Six million people in Somalia are facing acute hunger, with nearly two million children at emergency levels, as severe drought, conflict and falling humanitarian funding deepen what the UN describes as one of the world’s worst malnutrition crises. Medical charity MSF tells RFI it's sounding the alarm "before it's too late".

rfi.title: Violence against healthcare workers in DRC hampers Ebola response
rfi.description: Healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been coming under attack, the United Nations and Red Cross have warned, hampering efforts to stem the spread of the Ebola virus, which is spreading 'exponentially'.

rfi.title: Centre-left Glucksmann enters French presidential race as left tries to unite
rfi.description: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann has announced his candidacy for next year's presidential election, seeking to challenge hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon to lead France's fractured left, as a campaign increasingly dominated by the far right takes shape.

rfi.title: DRC and M23 rebels agree on roadmap for peace in eastern Congo
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the M23 rebel group have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks aimed at resolving the protracted conflict in eastern DRC. It marks the latest step in an internationally brokered peace process that has seen the parties make cautious concessions, without ending the fighting.

rfi.title: Saudi crown prince heads to France as Paris seeks closer Gulf ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Sunday for a two-day official visit, as Paris looks to deepen ties with Riyadh against a backdrop of war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Mystery elephant deaths in Kenya leave experts divided over cause
rfi.description: Conservationists and Maasai communities are calling for urgent answers as paralysis-like symptoms spread among elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park, with competing theories emerging over what is causing their deaths.

rfi.title: Togo says it has 'serious' evidence against detained French journalists
rfi.description: Togo's government says it has "serious and consistent evidence" against two French documentary filmmakers detained since July on charges of making false statements. Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani were arrested along with their Togolese fixer, Fred Vedomey, and have denied wrongdoing.

euronews.title: Canada hits back with new counter tariffs on US goods
euronews.description: "We will support our workers, our businesses and our industries with whatever it takes, for as long as it takes," Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said on Tuesday.

euronews.title: Mongolia positions itself as Asia's next data centre hub
euronews.description: During the COP17 conference in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia offered potential data centre investors tax relief, data security, cheap energy, land, and cold weather.

euronews.title: CIA director Ratcliffe arrives in Moscow on secret visit, US reports claim
euronews.description: John Ratcliffe reportedly arrived in the Russian capital on Tuesday for meetings, in what appears to be his first visit to Russia as CIA director.

euronews.title: Norway moves to tighten rules on use of smart glasses
euronews.description: Smart eyewear is a type of wearable tech offering features such as built-in cameras, microphones, and augmented-reality displays, allowing users to capture photos and videos or project data into view.

euronews.title: Azerbaijan's biggest bank enters Uzbek market with Davr Bank acquisition
euronews.description: Azerbaijan's largest financial institution, the International Bank of Azerbaijan, is expanding its corporate banking operations by acquiring a 51% controlling stake in Uzbekistan's Davr Bank in a deal valued at $150 million (€128.5m).

euronews.title: Eni's gas push in Egypt: $8.5 billion investment and 230 new wells
euronews.description: Eni strengthens its foothold in Egypt with 8.5 billion dollars of investments, 30 exploration wells and 200 development wells, focusing on Zohr, Denise West and Cyprus's Cronos project.

euronews.title: What is phubbing? The tech habit quietly damaging relationships
euronews.description: As our digital footprints grow, questions about digital privacy and tech habits are becoming more common between couples.

euronews.title: Trump slams Tehran for executing protesters at levels 'not seen before'
euronews.description: The US president said Tehran could no longer pay large segments of its military and was facing a "humanitarian crisis of epic proportions," days after 32 countries issued a joint statement condemning Iran's use of executions to silence dissent.

euronews.title: Spain to reform asylum laws to align with EU rules as Ceuta crisis remains unresolved
euronews.description: Spain is set to reform its immigration and asylum laws as the Ceuta crisis remains unresolved. Around 5,000 migrants, including 2,000 minors, remain in the enclave after the mass influx from Morocco in July.

euronews.title: Blacksmiths recreate Viking Age anchor using ancient techniques in Denmark
euronews.description: An international team of blacksmiths is recreating a Viking Age anchor using techniques and materials believed to have been used more than 1,000 years ago.

euronews.title: EXCLUSIVE: France wants to limit Ukraine's non-European procurement with EU money
euronews.description: France seeks time limits on Ukraine's derogations for non-EU defence purchases under €90bn loan, in push for European — and French — producers. Kyiv benefits from exemptions for Chinese and US parts.

euronews.title: Euronews exclusive: EU officials to travel to China as October deadline for trade rebalancing looms
euronews.description: Beijing and Brussels are at loggerheads after China barred its companies from cooperating with the European Commission in antitrust investigations. EU officials will travel to China in the coming days.

euronews.title: Phones, drones and ships running blind as GPS malfunctions across Poland
euronews.description: Poland's National Institute of Telecommunications has said that the source is external and linked to the activity of electronic warfare systems in the Baltic Sea region.

euronews.title: What to know as Greenland presents its forced contraception reports this week
euronews.description: The findings will arrive just one day after the Danish parliament is due to finalise compensation legislation for affected women, raising questions about how the reports’ assessment of responsibility will sit alongside Denmark’s existing response.

euronews.title: Qatar says officials working daily to revive US-Iran talks, urges Tehran to reopen Hormuz
euronews.description: Qatar says its officials are speaking to the parties daily to restart US-Iran negotiations, while urging Tehran to reopen and immediately restore freedom of navigation through the key energy route.

euronews.description: The rhetoric between the two countries is escalating, with Trump telling Canadian leaders on Monday to “fall in line” or face consequences “far WORSE” than existing tariffs.

euronews.title: Ceuta migration sparks nearly 9,600 hate posts on social media
euronews.description: The Spanish Observatory on Racism and Xenophobia logged 9,590 hate messages in two days tied to a July influx of some 80,000 migrants into Ceuta.

euronews.title: Meet the new James Bond villain? Saoirse Ronan is 'dead serious' about wanting to play a 007 baddie
euronews.description: This is not the first time that Oscar-nominated Irish actress Saoirse Ronan has expressed a desire to play a Bond villain... But with her recent comments and her husband currently rumoured to be the frontrunner for the next 007, we need this casting to happen now more than ever.

lemonde.description: Entre le 21 juillet et le 1ᵉʳ août, le mégafeu parti de Saumos a parcouru 42 000 hectares et détruit 240 maisons, surtout au Porge. Entre les habitants encore sous le choc, un climat de solidarité inédit s’est installé.

lemonde.description: Si l’ancien secrétaire général de l’Elysée, Alexis Kohler, s’est exprimé pour défendre le chef de l’Etat, les candidats issus du bloc central critiquent sa pratique du pouvoir tout en essayant de ne pas froisser son électorat.

lemonde.description: Pour son premier déplacement de campagne, le cofondateur du parti Place publique a choisi le thème de l’éolien. Aux côtés du sénateur Yannick Jadot, il a promis d’engager, dès sa victoire, cent jours de transformation pour « libérer la France » de « son addiction au gaz et au pétrole ».

lemonde.title: Fernando Cerimedo, l’éminence grise des dirigeants d’extrême droite latino-américains, emprisonné en Bolivie pour tentative de féminicide
lemonde.description: L’Argentin, proche collaborateur du président bolivien, a été arrêté dans l’est du pays après que son ex-compagne, l’avocate Nadia Beller, a été blessée par balles le 17 août. Le parquet soupçonne le stratège en communication et ancien conseiller de Jair Bolsonaro et Javier Milei d’être le commanditaire de l’agression.

lemonde.title: Dominique Méda, sociologue : « Les jeunes actifs se comportent envers les entreprises comme celles-ci se comportent à leur égard »
lemonde.description: Les personnes en début de carrière n’ont jamais été aussi nombreuses à vouloir se reconvertir, selon une étude du Céreq parue mardi. Dans un entretien au « Monde », la sociologue, coautrice de l’enquête, l’explique notamment par la rigidité du système scolaire et des conditions de travail dégradées.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : à Kramatorsk, le bilan s’alourdit à 21 blessés après les attaques russes de la nuit

lemonde.title: Le patronat et les syndicats tentent de relancer le dialogue pour faire avancer leur « agenda social autonome »
lemonde.description: Les organisations d’employeurs et de salariés se sont réunies lundi pour essayer de définir leur propre programme de négociations, sans directives gouvernementales. Alors qu’ils ne s’étaient pas revus dans une telle configuration depuis la fin janvier, les différents partenaires estiment nécessaire d’entretenir le dialogue social.

lemonde.description: Dominique Alderweireld, tenancier de maisons closes en Belgique, avait été relaxé, ainsi que Dominique Strauss-Kahn, aux côtés duquel il comparaissait, lors du procès pour proxénétisme, en 2015. Il est mort à l’âge de 77 ans à Tournai.

zeit.description: Israel werde keine Organisation dulden, die in das Hamas-Massaker verwickelt sei, kündigte die israelische Regierung an. Auf dem UNRWA-Gelände entstehe eine Schule.

Kerze als möglicher Auslöser: Fahrlässige Brandstiftung? Ermittlungen gegen Angestellte
Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: Stadt Magdeburg verschickt irrtümlich Hunderte Wahlscheine doppelt
zeit.description: In Magdeburg haben 440 Menschen ihre Briefwahlunterlagen doppelt erhalten. Das städtische Wahlamt erklärt sie für ungültig. Eine Mehrfachabstimmung sei nicht möglich.

zeit.title: Unfälle: U-Bahn-Unfall in Frankfurt – Ein Mensch verletzt
Zollkonflikt: Kanada: Vergeltungszölle gegen USA von bis zu 50 Prozent
Geheimdienste: US-Medien: CIA-Chef Ratcliffe zu Gesprächen in Moskau
Mutmaßlicher Brandanschlag: Möglicher Anschlag auf Drohnenfabrik in Slowakei verhindert
zeit.description: Die slowakische Polizei meldet, einen Anschlag auf eine Fabrik für unbemannte Flugobjekte vereitelt zu haben. Drei Verdächtige wurden gefasst, einer davon in Deutschland.

zeit.title: Spardruck in Brandenburg: Seniorenbeauftragter kümmert sich künftig auch um Behinderte
Befugnisse der Polizei: Kontroverse vor Anhörung zu neuem Polizeigesetz
John Ratcliffe: CIA-Direktor Ratcliffe soll zu Gesprächen in Moskau sein
zeit.description: Ein US-Militärflugzeug ist von Riga nach Moskau geflogen. An Bord befand sich Medienberichten zufolge CIA-Chef John Ratcliffe.

zeit.title: Wohnungsmangel: Hubertz kündigt Konzept für staatliche Wohnungsbaugesellschaft an
zeit.description: Das Kabinett will eine staatliche Wohnungsbaugesellschaft gründen, um Wohnungsmangel zu bekämpfen. Bundesbauministerin Verena Hubertz kündigte ein Konzept bis Herbst an.

zeit.title: Kabinettsklausur der Bundesregierung: Merz droht Hintermännern des Drohnenangriffs in Leipzig
zeit.description: Der Anschlagsversuch von Leipzig war wohl größer angelegt als angenommen. Bundeskanzler Merz kündigt eine harte Reaktion an. Und: VW-Chef Blume in Wolfsburg ausgepfiffen.

france24fr.title: Le patron de la CIA en visite à Moscou, selon des médias américains
france24fr.description: Selon les médias américains CBS et Axios, le patron de la CIA, John Ratcliffe, est en visite mardi à Moscou. Une annonce que ni le gouvernement américain ni le Kremlin n'ont jusqu'ici officiellement confirmé.

france24fr.title: Mélenchon, Glucksmann, Tondelier et les autres : combien de candidats à la présidentielle à gauche ?
france24fr.description: L’entrée dans la course à l’Élysée de Raphaël Glucksmann dans le cadre de la primaire socialiste, peut-être bientôt suivie par celles d’Olivier Faure et de Boris Vallaud, et par la candidature hors primaire du communiste Fabien Roussel illustrent la difficulté de s’y retrouver face à la pléthore de candidatures à gauche. France 24 fait le point.

france24fr.title: Après quarante-sept ans, la Syrie sort de la liste noire américaine
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois depuis quarante-sept ans, la Syrie ne figure plus sur la liste américaine des États soutenant le terrorisme. Une décision saluée par les autorités syriennes, qui espèrent qu'elle facilitera la reconstruction du pays et son retour sur la scène internationale. Récit de Marc Paupe.

france24fr.title: Iran : la tête de Barron Trump mise à prix dans une vidéo de propagande
france24fr.description: 🇮🇷 📺Dans une vidéo de propagande diffusée à la télévision d’État, l’Iran s’en prend à #Barron #Trump, le fils du président américain, et évoque une récompense de 10 millions de dollars pour sa mort.🇺🇸 Une nouvelle escalade dans les menaces visant la famille Trump, régulièrement ciblée par la République islamique.

france24fr.title: Au Kenya, un créateur de mode fait revivre le tissage traditionnel
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, un jeune créateur de mode mise sur des vêtements entièrement réalisés à la main pour se démarquer. Il utilise exclusivement des métiers à tisser manuels afin de préserver et de remettre au goût du jour des savoir-faire traditionnels menacés par l'industrialisation. Récit de Laurent Berstecher.

france24fr.title: Tchad : l'armée dénonce une nouvelle "violation du territoire"
france24fr.description: Le conflit au Soudan déborde de nouveau au Tchad. L'armée tchadienne affirme que des aéronefs et des drones liés aux belligérants soudanais ont poursuivi et bombardé une colonne de véhicules jusque sur le territoire tchadien. La correspondance à Ndjamena de Ghislaine Allahtaroum.

france24fr.title: Mali - Algérie : Abdoulaye Maïga à Alger pour relancer les relations
france24fr.description: Le chef du gouvernement malien, Abdoulaye Maïga, s'est rendu en Algérie ce lundi pour une visite de travail. Il a été reçu par le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune, dans un contexte de rapprochement après plusieurs années de tensions entre les deux pays. Correspondance de Serge Daniel.

france24fr.title: Guinée : au moins trente et un morts dans l'éboulement d'une décharge
france24fr.description: En Guinée, au moins trente et une personnes sont mortes dans l'éboulement d'une décharge. Le gouvernement affirme que "d'importants moyens matériels et humains ont été mobilisés" pour rechercher d'éventuelles personnes encore ensevelies. Le récit d'Emily Boyle.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Donald Trump annonce que le détroit d'Ormuz a été déminé
Sanctions américaines contre l’Iran : les Émirats cèdent et la Chine résiste
france24fr.description: Washington élargit ses sanctions contre l’Iran et ses partenaires commerciaux afin d’asphyxier les revenus du régime. Les Émirats arabes unis ont suspendu leurs échanges commerciaux et financiers avec Téhéran. À l’inverse, la Chine, premier acheteur du pétrole iranien, refuse de se joindre à cette campagne : Pékin promet de défendre ses intérêts et affirme que sa coopération avec l’Iran respecte le droit international. Décryptage de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: Sophie Adenot retourne dans l'espace pour une deuxième sortie extravéhiculaire
france24fr.description: Une semaine après sa première sortie extravéhiculaire historique, Sophie Adenot retourne hors de la Station spatiale internationale. La Française, accompagnée de l’astronaute américain Anil Menon, doit achever le remplacement d’une antenne de communication essentielle entre l’ISS et le centre de contrôle de Houston. Explications de notre journaliste Sylvain Rousseau.

france24fr.title: Espace : nouvelle sortie extravéhiculaire pour Sophie Adenot
france24fr.description: Sophie Adenot sort ce mardi dans l'espace pour la deuxième fois, afin de terminer sa mission restée inachevée il y a une semaine. Voici quelques images (accélérées) du début de cette sortie extravéhiculaire, destinée à remplacer une antenne de communication. Elle doit durer environ six heures et demie.

france24fr.title: Replay : Sophie Adenot effectue sa deuxième sortie dans l'espace
france24fr.description: L'astronaute française Sophie Adenot effectue sa deuxième sortie extra-véhiculaire, seulement une semaine après être devenue la première femme française à faire une sortie dans l'espace.

france24fr.title: Haïti : nouvelle attaque meurtrière attribuée à une coalition de gangs
france24fr.description: Au moins 47 personnes ont été tuées et 22 autres blessées lors d'une nouvelle attaque de gangs en #Haïti, selon un bilan provisoire de l’#ONU. La population dénonce le manque de protection face aux #violences répétées dans un pays en proie au chaos sécuritaire.

france24fr.title: Au Kenya, un jeune créateur de mode redonne vie au tissage traditionnel
france24fr.description: 🇰🇪 Au Kenya, un jeune créateur de mode mise sur le tissage manuel pour se démarquer. Il fabrique des tissus et des vêtements à la main, faisant revivre un savoir-faire traditionnel menacé par l’industrialisation.

france24fr.title: Une tornade d'une rare violence balaie un village en France
france24fr.description: Une tornade d’une rare violence a frappé lundi en fin d’après-midi le village de Pomas, près de Carcassonne. En moins de cinq minutes, le phénomène a fait 39 blessés, dont deux personnes en urgence absolue, et a détruit ou endommagé près de 300 habitations. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Sophie Adenot : une deuxième sortie dans l’espace pour achever sa mission
france24fr.description: Une semaine après être devenue la première Française à effectuer une sortie extravéhiculaire, Sophie Adenot retourne à l’extérieur de la Station spatiale internationale, à 400 kilomètres au-dessus de la Terre. Avec l’astronaute américain Anil Menon, elle doit achever le remplacement d’une antenne de communication entre l’ISS et le sol. Reportage de J.Benzina (France 2).

france24fr.title: Tchad : l’armée dénonce une nouvelle incursion liée à la guerre au Soudan
france24fr.description: Selon l’armée tchadienne, des aéronefs et des drones ont poursuivi et bombardé une colonne de véhicules jusque sur le territoire tchadien. Il s’agit de la quatrième incursion liée au conflit depuis le début de l’année.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Reformmüdigkeit der Deutschen ist eine Erzählung der Bundesregierung. Es fehlt das Vertrauen in die Politik
nzz.description: Die deutsche Regierung stolpert in die Reformunfähigkeit, weil sie Menschen nur belastet, ihnen aber keine positive Strategie bietet. Damit verspielt die schwarz-rote Koalition ihre Glaubwürdigkeit.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Selenski-Vertraute Irina Mudra muss in U-Haft +++ Lettland verbietet Einfuhr von Gütern aus Russland und Weissrussland
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Dies sind die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Weltfremde Gesetzgebung: Zu oft hat die EU jüngst die Schweiz und andere Drittstaaten vergessen
nzz.description: Viele Gesetze der EU dienen dem Zweck, die Welt zu verbessern. Zu oft hat sie jüngst damit aber Handelspartner vergrault. Das sollte beim nächsten grossen Vorhaben, das im Herbst ansteht, nicht passieren.

nzz.title: Washington erhöht den Druck – Teheran gibt sich unbeeindruckt
nzz.description: Das iranische Regime kann nicht darüber hinwegtäuschen, dass es wirtschaftlich stark unter Druck steht. Auf die Ankündigung neuer Sanktionen gegen die Islamische Republik und deren Handelspartner reagiert es aber betont gelassen.

nzz.title: Der Chip-Gigant im Zentrum des KI-Booms: Einmal mehr macht Nvidia die Börsen nervös
nzz.description: Für die Weltwirtschaft ist das Finanzergebnis von Nvidia so wichtig wie ein Zinsentscheid der US-Notenbank. Bei den Quartalszahlen muss unbedingt ein positives Ergebnis her, sonst droht ein Markteinbruch.

nzz.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi ist der Mathematiker unter den Lenkern im Mittelfeld – kann er bei Manchester City den Spanier Rodri ersetzen?
nzz.description: Grösser könnten die Erwartungen an einen 18-Jährigen kaum sein. Der Marokkaner kostet den englischen Klub 100 Millionen Euro Ablöse.

nzz.title: Ein Mann wütet im Kokainrausch im «Baur au Lac» und im Hotel «Storchen» – und richtet einen Schaden von 167 000 Franken an
nzz.description: Der Elektromonteur buchte Zimmer der Luxusklasse. Seine Taten will er im Verfolgungswahn begangen haben.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Zahl der Asylgesuche in der Schweiz nimmt weiter ab
In der Walliser Gemeinde Randa droht ein Gletscherabbruch am Weisshorn
nzz.description: Am Montagnachmittag kam es zu ersten Abbrüchen. Das betroffene Gebiet ist weiträumig gesperrt worden.

nzz.title: «Joyriding»: wenn riskantes Fahren zum tödlichen Social-Media-Trend wird
nzz.description: In Grossbritannien und Irland sind in den letzten Wochen zwölf Menschen bei Verkehrsunfällen ums Leben gekommen, mehrere davon im Zusammenhang mit jugendlichen Geisterfahrern, die für Social Media gefährliche Spritztouren filmen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Lage im Gazastreifen: Israel räumt Gelände des UN-Palästinenserhilfswerks +++ Beschuss tötet laut Sanitäter zwei Kinder
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Israel bombardiert Syrien und zielt auf die Türkei
nzz.description: Jerusalem folgt mit dem Angriff in Idlib einer neuen Doktrin und scheut dabei nicht die Konfrontation mit einem Nato-Staat. In Israel selbst regen sich Zweifel, ob die Rechnung aufgeht.

nzz.title: Fall Osman Kavala: Menschenrechtsgericht verurteilt Türkei
nzz.description: Bereits vor gut sieben Jahren hatte der Gerichtshof in Strassburg die Freilassung des türkischen Kulturförderers Kavala gefordert. Nun stellt das Gericht weitere Menschenrechtsverletzungen fest.

nzz.title: Die Basketballerin Sophie Cunningham war ein Nobody – mit ihrer Rhetorik gegen Trans-Athleten wurde sie über Nacht zum Star der amerikanischen Rechten
nzz.description: In der Frauen-Basketballliga WNBA tobt ein Kulturkampf. Konservative Kreise wehren sich dagegen, dass transsexuelle Athletinnen in der Liga partizipieren können – obwohl das noch nie vorgekommen ist. Die Spiele gleichen in diesen Tagen einem Zirkus.

nzz.title: Sie fressen alles weg und verwandeln Trockenmauern in Geröllhalden: Ziegenplage auf Capri
nzz.description: Ein Staatsanwalt, ein Starregisseur und neunzig Ziegen sind die Hauptdarsteller einer Sommergeschichte, die auf der Trauminsel im Golf von Neapel spielt.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Umbruch bei VW: Volkswagen-Chef Oliver Blume betont die Notwendigkeit der Sparmassnahmen +++ Die Chefin der Gewerkschaft bezeichnet das Vertrauen in den Konzernchef als beschädigt
nzz.description: Der VW-Chef Oliver Blume will den Konzern radikal umbauen, um ihn zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Belegschaft äussert bei den angelaufenen Betriebsversammlungen Kritik. Anfang September dürften erste Entscheide getroffen werden.

spiegel.title: Kanada verhängt Vergeltungszölle gegen USA von bis zu 50 Prozent
spiegel.description: Der Zollstreit zwischen den USA und Kanada geht in die nächste Runde. Nachdem US-Präsident Donald Trump neue 50-Prozent-Zölle ankündigte, gab sich Kanadas Premier Mark Carney kämpferisch. Nun kommt der Gegenschlag.

spiegel.title: Autonomes Fahren: Waymo plant Robotaxis in München ab 2027
spiegel.description: Google-Schwesterfirma Waymo plant, autonome Taxis in die bayerische Landeshauptstadt zu bringen. Schon bald sollen die ersten Testwagen unterwegs sein. Wie sicher ist das System und was erwartet die Fahrgäste?

spiegel.title: Vuelta: Radprofis flüchten vor Hagelsturm in ein Hotel und loben den Service
spiegel.description: Auf der Flucht vor einem Hagelsturm retteten sich die Radprofis auf der Spanienrundfahrt in ein Hotel. Nun erhält das Haus Bestbewertungen und Lob im Internet, auch für den »Handtuchservice«.

spiegel.title: Russland: CIA-Direktor John Ratcliffe zu Gesprächen in Moskau gelandet
spiegel.description: Zunächst war unklar, was es mit der US-Maschine auf dem Moskauer Flughafen auf sich hat. Nun berichten US-Medien, wer sich an Bord befand.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Volkswagen, Oliver Blume, Zuckersteuer, ChatGPT
spiegel.description: Der VW-Vorstand schwört die Belegschaft auf düstere Zeiten ein. Lars Klingbeil will auch alkoholfreie Biergetränke mit der Zuckersteuer belegen. Und OpenAI stoppt eine russlandfreundliche KI-Operation. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagabend.

spiegel.title: Social Design Award 2026: Letzter Aufruf für Ihre Projektidee
spiegel.description: Beim Leserwettbewerb des SPIEGEL suchen wir Initiativen und Projekte, die Menschen in Verbindung bringen und zum besseren Miteinander beitragen. Zu gewinnen sind 2 x 2500 Euro, die Einreichungsfrist endet am 31. August 2026.

spiegel.title: Mac mini und Mac Studio: Apple stellt neue Highspeed-Macs vor – und zieht die Preise weiter an
spiegel.description: Kurz bevor Tim Cook den Chefposten abgibt, kündigt Apple neue Macs und Chips an. Die Leistungswerte klingen vielversprechend. Die Preise nicht.

spiegel.title: Hannover 96 kritisiert Fans nach queerfeindlichen Beleidigungen
spiegel.description: In der ersten DFB-Pokalrunde spielte Hannover in Bremen, wo zeitgleich der CSD stattfand. Von einigen 96-Anhängern waren beim Spiel offenbar queerfeindliche Bedrohungen zu hören. Der Verein reagiert scharf.

spiegel.title: CTE im Football: Untersuchung zeigt Gehirnschäden bei vielen verstorbenen NFL-Spielern
spiegel.description: Die fortschreitende Gehirnerkrankung CTE könnte Profi-Footballer weit häufiger treffen als bisher angenommen. Darauf deutet eine Studie hin, für die Forschende die Gehirne toter Ex-Spieler untersucht haben.

spiegel.title: Mannheim: Getöteter Zugbegleiter wird mit Gedenktafel geehrt
spiegel.description: Serkan Çalar starb nach einer Prügelattacke. Eine Gedenkstätte am Mannheimer Hauptbahnhof soll künftig an den Zugschaffner erinnern.

spiegel.title: Taylor Swift: Wie der Popstar mit Druck und Überforderung umgeht
spiegel.description: Hohe Ambitionen, Kritik von außen, ständig unter Druck – das Leben im Rampenlicht kann Prominente überrollen. Taylor Swift verrät, was ihr in solchen Momenten hilft.

spiegel.title: CDU: Dennis Radtke wehrt sich gegen rechten Shitstorm nach Migrationsaussagen
spiegel.description: Aussagen des CDU-Europaabgeordneten Dennis Radtke zur Migration im ZDF lösen in den sozialen Medien heftige Reaktionen von rechts aus. Was hat er daraus gelernt?

spiegel.title: Armenien: Ex-Präsident Robert Kotscharjan wegen Korruptionsverdacht festgenommen
spiegel.description: Früher regierte er das Land, heute führt er Armeniens Opposition an: Robert Kotscharjan soll seine hohe Position für wirtschaftliche Vorteile ausgenutzt haben. Auch seine Söhne stehen unter Verdacht.

spiegel.title: Baden-Württemberg: Betrunkener Autofahrer verrät sich durch Schnarchen im Gebüsch
spiegel.description: Ein Mann wollte nach einer Alkoholfahrt offenbar seinen Rausch ausschlafen. Das wurde ihm zum Verhängnis: Durch Schnarchen machte er Polizisten auf sich aufmerksam.

spiegel.title: Florida: Mutter und Zweijährige vom Blitz erschlagen
spiegel.description: Ein Augenzeuge berichtet von einem orangen Schimmer: Im US-Bundesstaat Florida hat ein Blitz eine Frau und ihr Kind getroffen. Für sie kam jede Hilfe zu spät.

spiegel.title: MDR warnt mit schwarzem Bildschirm vor AfD: »Wie Sie sehen, sehen Sie nichts«
spiegel.description: Für einige Sekunden blieb es still: Der MDR warnt vor den Folgen einer Regierungsübernahme der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt – mit Aussetzern in Radio und Fernsehen.

spiegel.title: North West: Tochter von Kim Kardashian und Ye hat schon mehr als ein Dutzend Piercings
spiegel.description: Allein an den Händen hat North West mindestens zehn Piercings. Die würden sie vervollständigen, sagt die 13-Jährige. Zu einem Piercing sagen ihre Eltern Kim Kardashian und Kanye West jedoch Nein.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen: VW-Chef Oliver Blume stellt sich Belegschaft – Betriebsrat sieht Vertrauenskrise
spiegel.description: Wie soll es mit Volkswagen weitergehen: Konzernchef Blume stellte sich den Mitarbeitern und ihren Betriebsräten. Die erkennen in dem Termin keinen Fortschritt.

L’Union européenne a indiqué considérer «avec intérêt» l’éventuelle prochaine demande d’adhésion de l’Arménie. Le pays cherche à s'éloigner de Moscou, qui demande un référendum

L’artiste plasticien Gao Zhen a été condamné à 3 ans de prison pour avoir diffamé la mémoire du fondateur de la République populaire de Chine, à travers ses sculptures satiriques. Sous Xi Jinping, la Chine a fortement renforcé son Code pénal afin de sanctionner les atteintes au récit officiel

phys-org.title: The real reasons you procrastinate—and how to stop, according to science
phys-org.description: Faced with a task or project, do you repeatedly tell yourself that you'll do it "tomorrow," "soon" or "after watching just a few more videos"?

phys-org.title: Listening for extinction: Study finds areas of critical concern for northern spotted owls
phys-org.description: Northern spotted owl populations are approaching or have already crossed functional extinction across large areas of the Pacific Northwest, a new study, published in Ecological Applications found. Researchers used artificial intelligence and advanced monitoring methods to assess long-term trends at an unprecedented scale.

phys-org.title: Egypt's deserts were once home to a diverse shark community
phys-org.description: During the Late Cretaceous period, parts of Egypt were covered in water. A new study, published in the journal Cretaceous Research, describes new evidence that this tropical sea was home to a diverse community of sharks. The study adds five new species to the region's history, found in what the authors refer to as a "shark graveyard."

phys-org.title: How people treat you may shape your reputation and stabilize cooperation
phys-org.description: When one person helps, or refuses to help, another in public, this may change not only the provider's reputation but also the recipient's. A theoretical study led by Kobe University offers a simple explanation for how cooperation in large communities becomes stable and provides insights into phenomena like the bystander effect.

phys-org.title: Brazilians are MacGyver-ing their way around traditional markets
phys-org.description: Life hacks are everywhere on social media—people reuse everyday materials and objects to create ingenious solutions to common problems and needs.

phys-org.title: Climate change may halve omega‑3 fatty acids in fish and the organisms they eat
phys-org.description: You've probably heard that eating fish and other seafood is good for your health. One of the main reasons is that seafood is an excellent source of two important omega-3 fats called EPA and DHA.

phys-org.title: Nanoscale hairs may help gecko skin trap moisture and slow evaporation
phys-org.description: In a dry shrubland, a gecko sprints toward shelter. Its greatest danger is not a predator, although hawks circle overhead and sand cats wait in ambush. Rather, its most pressing concern is dehydration. Its skin is paper-thin; water can evaporate from its body into the dry air more quickly than it can replenish it. Fortunately, evolution has given it an adaptation: thin, nanoscopic hairs, called setulae, that cover its body and trap moisture.

phys-org.title: A tiny drop of water is all that's needed to find threatened frogs
phys-org.description: New James Cook University research has used highly sensitive environmental DNA (e-DNA) techniques to find two species of threatened frogs in places they've never been seen before—and find another still struggling to recover from past disease outbreaks. The research is published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice.

phys-org.title: Chatbots are making our writing more similar but losing the identity and personality behind it
phys-org.description: Large language models (LLMs) are making writing styles more similar without changing the overall meaning, according to an analysis of more than 880,000 texts across different writing types published in Nature Human Behaviour. The findings indicate that using LLMs could make it more difficult to identify important clues about aspects of a person's identity, personality and mental health from their language.

phys-org.title: Left‑handed people tend to be left‑leaning voters
phys-org.description: Political preferences are generally explained by income, age and level of education. However, our research suggests that a far more unexpected trait may also have a hand in how we vote. A survey carried out in 18 western countries has shown that left-handed people tend to identify more strongly with the political left. This finding appears to be more related to identity than biology.

phys-org.title: Families bear hidden costs of finding safety
phys-org.description: Led by La Trobe University, the research sheds light on a largely overlooked question in response to family violence: What does it cost families to become safe?

phys-org.title: Young golden eagles leave their parents' territory late
phys-org.description: When a young golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) finally leaves its parents' territory, it leaves behind the only safety net it has ever known. Until now, biologists had assumed that eagles took this step as soon as they could fly well enough to survive on their own.

phys-org.title: The hidden physics behind the shape of rose thorns
phys-org.description: Roses are known for their thorns, the sharp structures that can sting and prickle the skin. Thorns, botanically known as prickles, are thought to discourage animals from feeding on plants and may also help climbing roses grip other vegetation.

phys-org.title: The missing plants that could transform cities for people and nature
phys-org.description: Urban parks and public spaces need more shrubs and small trees to improve community well-being and support wildlife, University of Queensland researchers say.

phys-org.title: From nightlife to life at night: Cities must stay open later to beat the rising heat
phys-org.description: Summer in Europe is normally cause for celebration. Not this one, however, which will rank as one of the hottest on record. Wildfires have broken out everywhere from France to Greece, while intense drought has turned the grass in London's famous Hyde Park brown. This week, much of Europe is sweltering through yet another heat wave.

phys-org.title: AI financial advice can improve decisions or steer investors wrong, experiment finds
phys-org.description: To what extent can AI improve our financial decisions or steer us in the wrong direction? Researchers at the University of Bayreuth investigated this question in a new study involving 3,700 participants and fictional investment fund savings plans.

phys-org.title: 'Now boarding' … 240,000 miles from Earth, at the moon's first airport
phys-org.description: The moon's getting its first airport, and it's about to get busy. Within the next two decades, NASA's planned Gateway—humanity's first lunar spaceport—may become a bustling hub for Orion crew capsules, lunar landers, cargo vehicles and astronauts traveling between Earth, the moon and, eventually, destinations in the deep unknown.

phys-org.title: Probing issues relevant to students boosts civic engagement
phys-org.description: When social studies students delve into issues that affect their communities and discuss them in class, they are more likely to consider other people's points of view and are generally more interested in voting and other ways of participating in civic life.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: China’s Platform State and the AI Race
proj-syn.description: Balancing regulation with innovation is never easy, and the Chinese government’s robust support for AI could lead to inefficiency and excess. But the “platform state” model, combined with other strengths, has enabled China to achieve dominance in multiple strategic sectors, while enhancing its resilience.

proj-syn.title: Which Future for Online Life?
proj-syn.description: By articulating a vision of the future that seems inevitable, technology industry leaders want to create the impression that the surrender of privacy and other defining trends of the current moment cannot be stopped. But predictions become self-fulfilling prophecies only if we believe them and act accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Pro-Human Vision
proj-syn.description: The original vision of the internet as a democratizing force failed to account for the manner in which power would concentrate, attention would be monetized, and public discourse would be manipulated. In Europe and elsewhere, these lessons now must inform how we govern generative AI.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: Will We Preserve the Sources of Human Learning?
proj-syn.description: By obscuring or destroying the primary sources of knowledge, large language models create the illusion of an embodied and active collection of everything we know. But without examining and interrogating the human originators of recorded knowledge and wisdom, one cannot fully develop one’s own understanding.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.

crunchbase.title: Inside The Private-Market Divide: EquityZen’s Phil Haslett On AI, SaaS And Secondaries
crunchbase.description: The market for private-company shares has become a much bigger part of the startup ecosystem. In this Crunchbase News Q&A, EquityZen co-founder Phil Haslett discusses why startups are offering employees and investors liquidity earlier, and why secondary prices can be more revealing than headline valuations.

crunchbase.title: Why Bootstrapped Businesses Are More Relevant Than Ever
crunchbase.description: The traditional VC model funds a risky search for product-market fit, argues guest author Richard de Silva of Lateral Investment Management, while bootstrapped founders typically start with known customer problems, prioritize profitability and grow steadily from revenue rather than outside capital.

crunchbase.title: Startups Are Still Acquiring Startups, Led By Ultra-High-Valuation Unicorns

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Defense Tech, AI Tools And Infrastructure Lead The Way
crunchbase.description: The biggest financing of the week went to Castelion, a defense tech startup developing a hypersonic missile. Other sizable rounds went to companies developing AI inference technology, a video-creation platform, data centers and voice-to-text tools.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: AI For Everything From Recycling To Breathing To Winning Construction Bids
crunchbase.description: This month’s installment of this column is all AI, though applications for the technology range widely, from two startups that apply AI to trash or recycling, to another that promises to help people breathe and sleep better, to a company that says its AI can help architects and builders spot commercial projects before they’re even announced.

crunchbase.title: From Humanities To AI: How Ali Hussain Built Fintech Tabs Into A $400M Startup
crunchbase.description: Our third in a series of articles about non-tech founders getting venture funding features Tabs founder Ali Hussain, who started the AI fintech after realizing pursuing a Ph.D. in humanities was a terrible idea and spent some time in the tech workforce where he learned a few things about building venture-backed companies.

crunchbase.title: When Should A Board Consider Selling A Company?
crunchbase.description: The best boards continuously evaluate selling alongside scaling, pivoting, or staying independent, especially when the company is thriving, founder priorities are shifting, or strategic buyers begin showing interest, argues tech strategic adviser Itay Sagie. In this guest commentary, he share three signals that tell directors that it’s time to sell the company.

crunchbase.title: Which Investors Have Backed The Most 2026 Unicorns?
crunchbase.description: So far this year, 250 companies have joined the unicorn ranks through Aug. 15, up from 2025's 193 companies. Leading sectors included robotics, AI labs, healthcare and biotech, financial services, AI infrastructure, and AI deployment, among others. But which investors are winning the 2026 funding surge? We take a look.

crunchbase.title: VCs Pour Billions Into Physical AI As The Next Wave Of AI Investing Takes Shape
crunchbase.description: In the first half of 2026, global venture funding in the physical AI space totaled $47.4 billion across 521 deals, per Crunchbase data. That’s up dramatically — almost 4x — compared to the second half of 2025 when startups in the sector raised $12 billion across 470 deals.

crunchbase.title: Semiconductor Giants Are Busy Backing Startups This Year
crunchbase.description: Massive AI spending has helped push earnings and valuations for semiconductor industry leaders to record levels, prompting the sector's giants to invest record sums in artificial intelligence and robotics startups.
